summary: Merced County fire tower near Ballico, in use from the 1962 fire season and manned around the clock in 1975. FFLA lists it gone; no source gives a date or cause.

facts.design: Tower with a glass-walled cab of roughly 10 square feet
facts.status_note: FFLA California list marks it Gone; the sources read give no date or cause of removal

events.note: Fire committee authorized to look into installing a lookout station on the Barfield schoolhouse (February 12, 1948)
Present tower and station put into use for the 1962 fire season, replacing the Dickinson tower and the old Barfield station
Request from Fire Chief James Laginha for a radio base at the Barfield station lookout was granted
Station and tower crews on alert and manned 24 hours a day, per Engineer Bill Parsley and Engineer Eldron Thorton
County fire department gave Castle Air Force Base weather readings four times a day from the 65-foot tower, also used to spot fires

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1975 report gives a vantage point 50 feet above the rolling countryside; this is not a tower height. A 1983 note gives the tower as 65 feet. The record's 19.8 m equals 65 feet, so the record is kept.

notes_for_editor: Gone status rests on one FFLA list entry, with no date or cause in any source read, so the fate is thin. The Forest Lookouts page has nothing after 1983. Record ownership is unknown; the 1975 report calls it the only county-owned station with a fire lookout tower, so local ownership could be proposed for human review. Access level is left out of facts because no source read describes access today. A 2024 Merced County story about closing or merging fire stations names Ballico Station 92, but no source ties that station to this site, so it is not used. The FFLA list gives no NHLR registration for Barfield.
